condition:
Recreate Rocket League as closely as practical as a playable browser game. Preserve its recognizable third-person 3D presentation and the core car-soccer experience: drive and steer a rocket-powered car around an enclosed arena, accelerate, jump or boost, hit a large ball with spatial collisions, score into the opposing goal, receive clear goal and score feedback, and restart a match.

Before coding, research real Rocket League gameplay screenshots, official gameplay footage, and useful HUD or menu views. Select at least six high-signal visual anchors covering gameplay composition, camera, arena/environment, cars and ball, boost/trails and impact effects, and HUD or menus. Record every source URL and explain each selected anchor in the live progress page.

Use a real 3D scene with perspective, depth, 3D geometry, lighting, materials, and spatial collision; do not flatten it into a 2D or sprite-based substitute. Let the lead choose the implementation route and divide the work into independently judgeable pieces. Give each important piece a builder and a fresh-context critic. Have the critic inspect the actual running output, compare it directly with the references using side-by-side or blind A/B review when practical, identify the largest mismatch in silhouette, framing, scale, color, lighting, motion, interface placement, or interaction feedback, and send it back for improvement. Continue this loop until the result closely resembles the references or the run stops.

Maintain a live progress page with the reference URLs, screenshots or captures of the running result, current gaps, and the next improvement. Make controls and feedback observable and responsive: keyboard driving/steering, throttle/reverse, jump, boost, ball contact, goal detection, score/state display, win/lose or match-end state, and restart behavior.
